title: Longest palindromic subsequence
prompt:
Return the length of the longest subsequence of text that reads the same forwards and backwards.

- text has 0 to 1,000 lowercase English letters.
- This is an interval DP: solve every substring text[i..j] from short to long.
hints: Define L[i][j] as the answer for the substring from i to j inclusive.
If text[i] == text[j], both ends can wrap a palindrome: L[i][j] = L[i+1][j-1] + 2. Otherwise drop one end: max(L[i+1][j], L[i][j-1]).
Fill i from the end of the string backwards and j forwards from i, so smaller intervals are ready first. L[i][i] = 1.

solution.explanation: Matching end characters can always both be used as the outer pair of a palindrome. When they differ, at least one end is unused. Every state depends on strictly shorter intervals, so filling i downward and j upward respects the dependencies.

complexity.notes: Equivalent to the LCS of text and its reverse. Keeping only two rows reduces space to O(n).

followUps: What is the fewest characters to insert to make text a palindrome? (Hint: use this answer.)
